summary.text: Jason Janvrin is a Republican candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Rockingham 30, in the November 3, 2026 general election, after advancing from the September 8 primary.
He is a U.S. Army veteran who served in the New Hampshire House in three earlier stints between 2016 and 2024.

paragraphs.text: Janvrin served in the U.S. Army from 1991 to 2013.
He earned a high school diploma from Winnacunnet High School in 1990, an associate degree from Hesser College in 1994 and a bachelor's degree from the University of New Hampshire in 2002.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as government administration, and says he has chaired the Seabrook Municipal Planning Board and served on the Seabrook Municipal Budget Committee.
Janvrin represented Rockingham 20 from 2016 to 2018 and Rockingham 37 from 2018 to 2020, and he held the Rockingham 40 seat from December 7, 2022, to December 4, 2024.
According to Ballotpedia, his committee assignments included the House Judiciary Committee and, in 2023-2024, the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Janvrin described himself as a three-term representative who has taken time away.

He listed his campaign messages as defense of the Second Amendment, his role as prime sponsor of a law prohibiting credit cards from being used to track firearm purchases, and a view that current New Hampshire abortion law is a balance that is working.
